cells.tense: You are moving right now with the sense that this one is settled.
cells.ask: Name the piece you are nearly done with, decide the one thing that finishes it, and do that thing today.
cells.core:
The shape is clear and it shows in how you work — the calls get made before the long debate, and the people around you get the version you actually mean. Nothing here needs another draft of the plan.

The one thing left is what finishing costs. There is a last piece sitting there because after it there is nothing to add, and adding is the part you are good at. Naming it out loud — the last email, the final cut, the number you keep not writing down — does as much as the doing. Do it and let it stand as is, without the closing pass nobody asked for. The balance you have carries a price, and the price is deciding.
cells.sheetLine: You know what finishing costs, and you can pay it.

cells.place: the handover of a finished piece, where the next one starts.

cells.tense: You are finishing something in your head before it has actually been made.
cells.ask: Pick the one thing you keep reworking past done and stop work on it. Hand it over as it stands.
cells.core:
You want the end in hand before the thing is made. There is a version in your head of how it will land, and you keep working toward that instead of toward what is actually here and moving. That is what puts you out in front of your own timing.

It shows up in details that do not need more detail, drafts that get one more pass, and then one more after that. The finishing is real — the drag is you reaching the end before the work has gotten there. Let a piece stop where it stopped. What you actually have is the ability to see what is finished; use it for that rather than for imagining what could still go wrong. Send the thing out as it stands today.
cells.sheetLine: You keep finishing something you already finished.

cells.tense: You are still standing in a doorway the work already walked through.
cells.ask: Take one finished thing off your list by giving it to the person who needs it, without another pass.
cells.core:
The work is done and you are not walking out of it. The piece sits there and you stand one step before the end, with the handover right in front of you and not happening.

Done well, this is the clean part: a finished thing set down whole, nothing held back, the next piece already taking up the room it needs. What gets you there is starting the next small thing, not mustering more effort at the old one. Begin the next rough version smaller than the old one and leave the old one alone. The piece you are holding does not need a better final line. It needs your hand off it.
cells.sheetLine: The work is done. You are the one still in the doorway.
cells.verb: carrying something through to the point where it is done.

cells.tense: You are already deciding what the work becomes, and you call it what happened.
cells.ask: Name one thing you just finished that you have been describing as what happened. Own it as your decision.
cells.core:
You are already shaping how this closes — you see the crossing point before anyone else, and the work moves toward what you point at. Ask around and they will say the thing went that way, as if it decided for itself. The author is in the room; only the name is missing.

What is real is that you can see it, and it only counts once you say it out loud. Keeping it as fact lets you stay above the work and skip the decision, which leaves nothing for anyone to meet you in. Endings go clean when you let them own you. The ending you already chose is clear in the room; your call is the piece that is missing.
cells.sheetLine: You are deciding how this turns out. Say it out loud.
